title: trifolium filiforme subsp. dubium
intro: Trifolium filiforme subsp. dubium, commonly known as False or woodland white clover, is a perennial plant native to North America, characterized by its small white flowers and trifoliate leaves. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may aid in reducing inflammation and protecting against oxidative stress. Therapeutically, Trifolium filiforme subsp. dubium is believed to exhibit actions such as antimicrobial and antifungal activities, as well as potential anti-cancer properties. The plant's bioactive constituents include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal effects and have been studied for their potential applications in treating various health conditions.
